CHAPTER XIV PROCEDURE FOR LICENSING, ISSUANCE OF ELECTRONIC SALES TAX INVOICES AND INTEGRATION OF REGISTERED PERSONS > Rule 150R
CHAPTER XIV-AD PROCEDURE FOR SEALING AND DE-SEALING OF BUSINESS PREMISES OF TIER-1 RETAILERS > Rule 150ZER

questions.reference: Yes. Under Rule 150Q(3), retailers whose withholding tax deductible under section 236G or 236H in the preceding period exceeds Rs. 100,000 or Rs. 500,000 respectively must integrate. This was added by SRO 2071(I)/2025 of 3 November 2025 and is not in the May 2025 Chapter XIV.
questions.standalone_question: Does a retailer have to integrate with FBR because of the withholding tax deducted from it, and what is the threshold?
questions.answer:
Yes. Under rule 150Q(3), retailers whose deductible withholding tax under sections 236G or 236H of the Income Tax Ordinance, 2001, during the immediately preceding period exceeds one hundred thousand rupees or, as the case may be, five hundred thousand rupees, are required to integrate their business, for the purposes of clause (g) of sub-section (43A) of section 2 of the Sales Tax Act, 1990 [1][3]. The sub-rule was added by S.R.O. 2071(I)/2025 dated 3 November 2025 [3]. The documents do not say which retailers fall under the Rs 100,000 limit and which under the Rs 500,000 limit.

This is not legal advice; check the cited rule.
questions.verdict_reason: The answer gives Rule 150Q(3), the Rs 100,000 and Rs 500,000 thresholds under sections 236G/236H, and SRO 2071(I)/2025 of 3 November 2025, matching the reference. Its hedge on which threshold applies to which section is less precise than the reference's 'respectively', and it omits the May 2025 Chapter XIV note, but neither contradicts the reference.
unsupported_claims: A retailer is required to integrate with FBR because of the withholding tax deducted from it.

retrieval.question: Should our system create the digital invoice when we bill the customer or when they pay?

retrieved.section: CHAPTER XIV PROCEDURE FOR LICENSING, ISSUANCE OF ELECTRONIC SALES TAX INVOICES AND INTEGRATION OF REGISTERED PERSONS > Rule 150R
1. What is the Digital Invoicing System?

questions.reference: At the time of supply: for goods, delivery or receipt of payment, whichever is earlier (section 2(44)); for services, when they are rendered.
questions.standalone_question: Should our system create the digital invoice when we bill the customer or when they pay?
questions.answer:
Neither strictly: digital invoices must be issued at the time of supply, i.e. the receipt of payment or the delivery of goods, whichever is earlier, as provided under Section 2(44) of the Sales Tax Act, 1990 [1]. So if the customer pays before delivery, the invoice is due at payment; if delivery happens first, it is due at delivery. The documents do not say that the billing date itself triggers invoicing.

This is not legal advice; check the cited rule.
questions.verdict_reason: The answer correctly gives the goods rule (time of supply = earlier of delivery or receipt of payment, section 2(44)), but it omits the reference's point that for services the invoice is due when they are rendered.

questions.reference: You become liable to penalties under section 33 of the Sales Tax Act (Rule 150X).
questions.standalone_question: What happens to us if we miss the digital invoicing integration deadline?
questions.answer:
If you are notified and miss the integration deadline, you are liable to penal action under section 33 of the Sales Tax Act [1][2]. You may seek an extension under the relevant rules, but if you do not integrate by the extended deadline (or contravene any provision of the Act), section 33 penalties apply [1]. Registered persons failing to comply with the Board's integration timelines are likewise liable to the penalties defined in section 33 [2]. The documents do not state the specific penalty amounts.

This is not legal advice; check the cited rule.

retrieval.question: We issued a digital invoice but the customer returned the goods. How do we cancel or correct it?

retrieved.section: CHAPTER XIV PROCEDURE FOR LICENSING, ISSUANCE OF ELECTRONIC SALES TAX INVOICES AND INTEGRATION OF REGISTERED PERSONS > Rule 150R
CHAPTER III CREDIT AND DEBIT NOTE AND DESTRUCTION OFGOODS > Rule 20
CHAPTER III CREDIT AND DEBIT NOTE AND DESTRUCTION OFGOODS > Rule 19

questions.reference: Issue a debit or credit note under section 9 of the Sales Tax Act and make the corresponding adjustment against output tax in the return, subject to the Board's conditions; the mechanism, including electronic adjustments, is prescribed by the Board.
questions.standalone_question: We issued a digital invoice but the customer returned the goods. How do we cancel or correct it?
questions.answer:
Under Section 9 of the Sales Tax Act 1990, if goods are returned or supply is cancelled so that the amount on the tax invoice needs modifying, the registered person may, subject to the Board's conditions and limitations, issue a debit or credit note and make the corresponding adjustment against output tax in the return [1][2]. Issuance of debit and credit notes is governed by the mechanism, including electronic adjustments, prescribed by the Board [2]. Under Rule 19, where a supply or part of it is cancelled or returned, the buyer/recipient issues a Debit Note (in duplicate) showing the quantity returned or cancelled, its value as per the original tax invoice, and the related sales tax paid [6]. The note must include the name and NTN of the recipient and supplier, the number and date of the original sales tax invoice, the reason for issuance, and the signature and seal of the authorized person; the original goes to the supplier and the duplicate is retained [5][6]. If the goods were returned by an unregistered person, the supplier issues a credit note with the same particulars, only with the prior approval of the Commissioner [5]. Your POS/e-invoicing software must record every adjustment, modification or cancellation with logs for each activity [4].

This is not legal advice; check the cited rule.
questions.verdict_reason: The answer states that a debit or credit note is issued under section 9 with a corresponding adjustment against output tax, subject to the Board's conditions, and under the Board's prescribed mechanism including electronic adjustments; it adds no contradictions.
